title: Getting hired without politics; reading music from Professor Valentine
summary: Callender says he got work because he could read anything, thanks to theory and harmony taught before he touched an instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did you need an in? Did you need somebody to bring you in? You weren't just hired because you were a good bass player? Were you? I mean, in that time didn't you have to know somebody or somebody make arrangements for you to get the gig? Or not?
Well, no, it didn't happen exactly like that. I guess they thought I was a good bass player, so they hired me.
Good! Because I've talked to a lot of musicians who say all kinds of politics sometimes had to be done through.

Well, a lot of politics does go on. But I've never been a politician. I guess I've just happened to be in some of the right places at the right time. So that's what getting with... Playing with Louis Armstrong at that

time I consider a stroke of luck, because I just happened to be in the right place, and they needed a bass player who can read, and fortunately, I could read anything they'd put up. I always... I could read before I could play. My teacher in Bordentown, New Jersey, Professor Valentine, who happened to be a friend of W.C. Handy's, taught me theory and harmony and counterpoint before I ever picked up an instrument. So I was fortunate in that way. I knew the keyboard, too.
